turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so I have about twenty minutes. Owen found out he got a zero from the gradebook on his phone, in the middle of class, and nobody called me first. Explain that.
Thanks for coming in, Ms. Kalinowski.
I didn't come to be thanked. You asked for this meeting, so start with who decided on the zero, and whether anyone spoke to Owen before it went in.
The school's AI checker flagged Owen's essay at 94 percent.

That's a machine's guess, and the company that sells it says it shouldn't be the only basis for punishing a student. I'm writing down that your reason is a percentage. What else do you have, or is that all of it?
That's very high. The software is quite reliable.

Reliable according to whom? Fourteen detection tools were tested in one study and found "neither accurate nor reliable", and your own school's procedure says software results don't by themselves establish a concern. Which of those did you follow before entering the zero?
So I had to give him a zero.
"Had to." Under which section of your procedure? Because the one I printed says you call me before any mark goes in, and I'm still waiting to hear that call happened.
I hope you understand my position.
"Hope." Hope isn't a document, Hale. The zero comes off, you apologise to Owen, and if it doesn't, I'm going to the principal when we're done here.
